FL-2027-SB40.title: Relief of H.H. by the Department of Children and Families
FL-2027-SB40.summary: Relief of H.H. by the Department of Children and Families; Providing for the relief of H.H. by the Department of Children and Families; providing an appropriation to compensate H.H. for injuries and damages sustained as a result of the negligence of the department; providing legislative intent; providing a limitation on compensation and the payment of certain fees and costs, etc. CLAIM WITH APPROPRIATION: $14,926,640
FL-2027-SB40.policyArea: general relief bills and local relief bills (claims bills)
FL-2027-SB40.aiSummary: The bill would provide relief for H.H. by the Department of Children and Families and set aside money to pay for injuries and damages tied to the department’s negligence. It would provide $14,926,640 in compensation and set limits on that payment and on some fees and costs.

FL-2027-SB26.title: Relief of the Estate of Oscar Cabrera and Stephanie Cabrera by Miami-Dade County
FL-2027-SB26.summary: Relief of the Estate of Oscar Cabrera and Stephanie Cabrera by Miami-Dade County; Providing for the relief of the Estate of Oscar Cabrera and Stephanie Cabrera, as personal representative and surviving widow, by Miami-Dade County; providing an appropriation to compensate the Estate of Oscar Cabrera and Stephanie Cabrera for damages due to the wrongful death of Mr. Cabrera as a result of the negligence of Miami-Dade County; providing a limitation on compensation and the payment of attorney fees, etc. CLAIM: $4,024,441
FL-2027-SB26.policyArea: general relief bills and local relief bills (claims bills)
FL-2027-SB26.aiSummary: The bill would provide money from Miami-Dade County to the estate of Oscar Cabrera and Stephanie Cabrera to cover damages tied to Mr. Cabrera’s wrongful death. It would set a limit on the payment, including attorney fees. The claim amount is $4,024,441.

FL-2027-SB12.title: Relief of Odalys Fortes, Pablo Becerra, and Aliyah Isabel Mieryteran by Miami-Dade County
FL-2027-SB12.summary: Relief of Odalys Fortes, Pablo Becerra, and Aliyah Isabel Mieryteran by Miami-Dade County; Providing for the relief of Odalys Fortes, Pablo Becerra, and Aliyah Isabel Mieryteran by Miami-Dade County; providing for an appropriation to compensate Ms. Fortes, Mr. Becerra, and Ms. Mieryteran for injuries sustained as a result of the negligence of Miami-Dade County; providing a limitation on compensation and the payment of attorney fees, etc. CLAIM: Indeterminate
FL-2027-SB12.policyArea: general relief bills and local relief bills (claims bills)
FL-2027-SB12.aiSummary: Miami-Dade County would be required to pay money to Odalys Fortes, Pablo Becerra, and Aliyah Isabel Mieryteran for injuries tied to the county’s negligence. It also sets limits on the compensation and on lawyer fees.

FL-2026-HB4041.title: Compensation for Health Care Services for Inmates in Indian River County
FL-2026-HB4041.summary: Compensation for Health Care Services for Inmates in Indian River County; Limits compensation to health care provider that provides any medical services for inmate housed in Indian River County detention center under certain conditions; requires certain compensation for specified hospital that provides medical services for specified inmates if hospital does not have contract with county to provide such services; limits compensation to entity that provides emergency medical transportation services for inmate housed in Indian River County detention center if entity does not have contract with county to provide such services.

FL-2026-SB1452.aiSummary: The law changes several Department of Financial Services rules on reports, payroll timing, and public fund chart-of-accounts reporting. It also changes who can qualify for a hurricane mitigation inspection under the My Safe Florida Home Program, treats cash redemptions and debit card redemptions the same, and updates when certain business interests are considered abandoned. It also ratifies some rules about legal tender.

FL-2026-HB505.title: Virtual Currency Kiosks
FL-2026-HB505.summary: Virtual Currency Kiosks; Revising the requirements for certain rules adopted by the Financial Services Commission; revising the actions by money services businesses, authorized vendors, or affiliated parties which constitute grounds for disciplinary action; prohibiting persons from engaging in certain business unless they are registered or exempt from registration; prohibiting a virtual currency kiosk business from operating in this state without registering or renewing its registration; requiring the Office of Financial Regulation to give a specified notice to applicants; specifying that certain money transmitters are exempt from registration as a virtual currency kiosk business but are subject to certain provisions; requiring applicants to submit certain information to the office to be registered as a virtual currency kiosk business; requiring a virtual currency kiosk business to ensure that its virtual currency kiosk requires certain attestations from the customer and displays a certain disclosure; requiring a virtual currency kiosk business to provide a customer with a specified physical or electronic receipt upon completion of a virtual currency transaction; requiring a virtual currency kiosk business to issue a full refund under certain circumstances, etc.

FL-2026-HB505.aiSummary: The law changes rules for virtual currency kiosks and the businesses that run them in Florida. It says these businesses must register or renew their registration, give certain notices and information to the state office, show customer warnings at the kiosk, give a receipt after each transaction, and give a full refund in some cases. It also changes when money services businesses and related parties can face discipline and says some money transmitters are exempt from kiosk registration but still follow certain rules.
